cf.title: Allow bare library names for non-superuser LOAD

input.subject: [PATCH] Allow bare library names for non-superuser LOAD

verdict_reasoning: The goal is modest and no objection is fatal. The open point is standards-compat-1: after the patch, `LOAD 'demo'` loads `$libdir/demo` for a superuser and `$libdir/plugins/demo` for other roles, with no message. Message #6 shows the case, and the answer in message #7 was not accepted in message #8. demand-1 is a secondary point: convenience is the only stated motive, and the explicit prefix works today.

brief.title: Expand bare library names to $libdir/plugins for non-superuser LOAD
brief.problem: Non-superusers may LOAD only libraries in $libdir/plugins, and they must write that prefix explicitly, as in LOAD '$libdir/plugins/mylib'. The author finds this inconvenient and inconsistent with local_preload_libraries, which prepends $libdir/plugins to bare names.
brief.proposed_design: The patch moves the $libdir/plugins expansion from load_libraries() into load_file(), so every restricted load handles bare names the same way. When a non-superuser runs LOAD with a bare file name, Postgres prepends $libdir/plugins/. Names with a path must still begin with exactly that string.
user_visible_surface: LOAD 'name' run by a non-superuser now resolves a bare name to $libdir/plugins/name instead of failing.
The same LOAD 'name' resolves to different files for a superuser and a non-superuser when both directories hold a library of that name.
A non-superuser LOAD of a bare name not present in plugins now fails with "could not access file" instead of "access to library ... is not allowed".
The LOAD reference page documents the automatic prefix.
author_claims: Writing the $libdir/plugins/ prefix is inconvenient for non-superusers.
The change makes LOAD consistent with local_preload_libraries.
Documenting the expansion is enough to justify the changed error message.
Admins should avoid installing different libraries with the same name, which removes the ambiguity concern.
brief.thread_state: Japin Li and solai v found the patch fine, and solai v tested that path escapes are still rejected. Jim Jones objected that the same command loads different files per role, accepted the error-message change if documented, and left the role-dependent semantics open.
unclear: The proposal does not say whether the new error for a missing plugin uses a different SQLSTATE than before.
The commit message does not say whether superuser LOAD or session_preload_libraries behavior changes in any way.
The thread does not say whether the role-dependent resolution should warn, error on ambiguity, or stay silent.
The patch adds no regression tests, judging from the touched-file list.
search_queries: LOAD access to library not allowed

objections.title: Same LOAD string resolves to different files depending on role
objections.failure_scenario: An admin tests a setup script as superuser, where `LOAD 'demo'` loads `$libdir/demo`. The same script run by an application role, or after `SET ROLE`, loads `$libdir/plugins/demo` without any message. Before the patch that run failed with an error, as message #6 shows with auto_explain.
objections.argument: local_preload_libraries prepends `$libdir/plugins` for every role, so it does not depend on the role. The patch makes one LOAD string mean two paths depending on `superuser()`, so the consistency claim holds only for the restricted branch. Message #7 answers that admins should not install same-named libraries, and message #8 calls this trading a server guarantee for admin discipline. The thread did not settle the point, and nothing in the proposal detects or reports the ambiguity.
objections.author_must_show: Why not resolve bare names the same way for all roles, or raise an error when the name exists in both `$libdir` and `$libdir/plugins`?

critic.reasoning: Message #6 reproduces the case, and message #8 leaves it open after the author's reply in #7. local_preload_libraries is restricted for every role, so the existing practice the patch copies does not cover role-dependent resolution in LOAD.

objections.title: No user demand shown for dropping the $libdir/plugins/ prefix
objections.failure_scenario: A deployment where the same library name exists in $libdir and $libdir/plugins sees LOAD 'name' pick a different file per role, as message #6 shows. Admins learn this when a script that worked as superuser loads another module under a normal role. The users who gain only skip typing a fixed prefix.
objections.argument: The only stated need is the author's view that the prefix is inconvenient (message #3), and Japin Li called it "a bit inconvenient" (message #4). No field report or -general request is cited, and no non-superuser workflow is shown that the prefix blocks. The workaround is to write '$libdir/plugins/name', which works today and is documented. The cost of role-dependent resolution and a changed error falls on admins and scripts that never asked for the shortcut.
objections.author_must_show: Which users or tools run non-superuser LOAD of plugins today, and where has the explicit prefix caused them real trouble?

critic.reasoning: The thread gives convenience as the only motive (messages #3 and #4), and the explicit prefix does the job. The cost is small and falls mostly on users of bare names, so this is a show-demand point and no reason to reject.

refuted.title: Role-dependent resolution of LOAD becomes a permanent contract
refuted.failure_scenario: An admin installs demo.so in both $libdir and $libdir/plugins. A deploy script runs LOAD 'demo' as the owner role, which is later changed from superuser to non-superuser. The same command now loads a different library with no error or warning, and the admin finds out only from changed behavior.
refuted.argument: Message #6 shows the same LOAD 'demo' loading passwordcheck for a superuser and auto_explain for a normal role, where today the normal role gets an error. Message #7 answers that admins should not install same-named libraries, and message #8 notes this trades a server guarantee for admin discipline. That point stayed open. Once released, scripts will rely on bare names, so the project cannot later make the ambiguous case an error.
refuted.author_must_show: Why should an ambiguous bare name resolve silently, instead of raising an error when $libdir and $libdir/plugins both hold a library of that name?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-1. The added claim that the project could never later make the ambiguous case an error has no support in the material.

refuted.title: Demand rests on one convenience report
refuted.failure_scenario: The project changes documented LOAD semantics and an error class that monitoring may match, as message #6 notes. The only gain is that non-superusers skip a typed prefix. Few sites let non-superusers load plugins at all, so the change may serve almost no one.
refuted.argument: Message #3 gives convenience as the only motive, and message #2 points out the current rule is documented on purpose. The thread has no field report, no -general request, and no case where the explicit prefix blocked a real deployment. Message #4 does not say whether the asymmetry with local_preload_libraries was intended. This is a not-now point, and evidence of demand would change it.
refuted.author_must_show: Which deployments let non-superusers LOAD plugins today, and where has the explicit $libdir/plugins/ prefix caused real trouble for them?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of demand-1. This version also says few sites allow non-superuser LOAD and that the rule is documented "on purpose", and the thread supports neither statement.

refuted.title: Explicit $libdir/plugins/ prefix already does the job
refuted.failure_scenario: A script run by both a superuser and an ordinary role uses LOAD 'demo' instead of the explicit path. It loads different files per role. The admin finds out only when the extension behaves differently, as message #6 shows. The explicit form LOAD '$libdir/plugins/demo' never has this problem.
refuted.argument: Non-superusers can already load any library in plugins by writing LOAD '$libdir/plugins/name'. Message #5 confirms this works today, so the gain is about 16 fewer characters. The author's reasons are convenience (message #3) and consistency with local_preload_libraries (message #1). The current documented rule, that the name must begin with exactly that string, makes one command name one file for every role, and the shortcut gives that up.
refuted.author_must_show: Which users or tools have hit the explicit-prefix requirement in practice, and why is typing the prefix not acceptable for them?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of demand-1, which already states that the explicit prefix works today and asks the same question. Its failure scenario repeats standards-compat-1.

touch_points.label: security / privileges
touch_points.reason: The patch changes the path check in load_file() that limits non-superuser LOAD to `$libdir/plugins`.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: Role-dependent resolution of a bare LOAD name becomes documented behavior that later changes must keep.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)
touch_points.reason: `LOAD '$libdir/plugins/name'` already gives non-superusers the same result today.

questions: Why not resolve bare names the same way for all roles, or raise an error when the name exists in both `$libdir` and `$libdir/plugins`?
Which users or tools run non-superuser LOAD of plugins today, and where has the explicit prefix caused them real trouble?
Does the new "could not access file" error for a missing plugin carry a different SQLSTATE than the old "access to library ... is not allowed" error?
Does moving the expansion into load_file() change superuser LOAD or session_preload_libraries in any way?

committability.owner_note: Someone who knows the dynamic loader code in dfmgr.c and the preload library settings would have to own it. No committer is identified in the visible thread.
committability.liability: The owner signs for LOAD semantics that depend on the role and for a changed error on a missing plugin. Both are user-visible and hard to change once scripts use bare names.
committability.author_follow_up: The author answered review comments on the same day in message #3 and again in message #7. Nothing is said about fixes after commit.

priority.reason: The patch is 3.8 KB across load.sgml, dfmgr.c and miscinit.c, and it helps only sites where non-superusers LOAD plugins. The role-dependent resolution from message #6 needs an agreed answer before code review is useful.

provisional_note: Without the code, I could not check how the patch detects a bare name, including Windows path separators, or whether dynamic_library_path is ever consulted. Only 3 of 8 messages were read directly.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: document an example to set multiple libraries in shared_preload_libraries
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a documentation example showing how to set multiple libraries in shared_preload_libraries, because some syntax forms pass ALTER SYSTEM but stop the server from starting after a restart. Discussion moved toward documenting list quoting in the "Parameter Names and Values" section, and toward having ALTER SYSTEM check that the libraries exist.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. The author asked whether the examples should use postgresql.conf syntax or ALTER SYSTEM syntax, since the quoting rules differ, and the visible messages do not answer this. Later messages argued that documentation alone is not enough and proposed a stat() check in ALTER SYSTEM, but no revised patch appears.

precedents_retrieved.title: warn if GUC set to an invalid shared library
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch emits a WARNING when ALTER SYSTEM, ALTER ROLE or ALTER DATABASE sets shared_preload_libraries, session_preload_libraries or local_preload_libraries to a library file that cannot be found, with a DETAIL saying the server or new sessions will fail to start. It also adds a CONTEXT line naming the setting and the config file line when startup fails on a missing library, and still allows setting the value before the library is installed.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author did not answer Heikki Linnakangas's November 2024 review, so the entry was returned with feedback after four weeks. That review asked for examples of what is accepted and when the warnings appear, and asked about documentation. It also noted that the new PGC_S_TEST_FUNCTION source was missing from GucSource_Names, and it suggested a separate is_testing flag as another design. Robert Haas and Heikki both said the thread needed too much context to review, and an earlier step that switched ALTER SYSTEM to PGC_S_TEST was dropped because it would let invalid values into postgresql.auto.conf.

precedents_retrieved.title: Mingw: Fix import library extension, build actual static libraries
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changes MinGW builds to give import libraries the .dll.a extension instead of .a, matching downstream workarounds in Fedora and Arch Linux packages. A second patch builds real static libraries next to the DLLs, which it describes as modeled on the AIX case in Makefile.shlib.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Peter Eisentraut found nothing in the MinGW documentation to support the .dll.a naming, since its examples match the current naming, and he asked the author for a source. Noah Misch pointed out that Postgres does not build static libraries on AIX, so the premise of the second patch was wrong. He also noted that static and import libraries would need different names. The visible thread shows no reply from the author before the entry was returned with feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_regress.c: Fix "make check" on Mac OS X: Pass DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes pg_regress pass DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH explicitly to the shell commands it runs on macOS, because System Integrity Protection removes that variable and "make check" then cannot load libpq from the temporary install. It adds a global extra_envvars string that is empty elsewhere and holds "DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH=..." on macOS.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The patch fixes only pg_regress, but other test suites hit the same problem, so a fix would need changes potentially everywhere system() is called. Tom Lane said a patch that does not handle all test cases from "make check-world" would not get much support. David Zhang's tests showed isolation and TAP tests still fail, and the visible messages contain no updated patch from the author.

precedents_retrieved.title: pglogical_output - a general purpose logical decoding output plugin
precedents_retrieved.summary: Craig Ringer proposed pglogical_output as a contrib module for 9.6: a general-purpose logical decoding output plugin that streams changes in a documented binary or JSON protocol. It adds client-negotiated startup parameters, a relation metadata cache, and C and PL/pgSQL hooks for filtering rows and origins.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andres Freund's late review found design problems. He objected to the PL/pgSQL hooks, because output plugins may not access normal tables, and to having two output formats in one plugin. He also argued that the relation metadata cache is not safe against cache invalidations and that api_private leaks memory. Craig Ringer agreed to rework several of these points, but the SGML documentation was still unfinished, and Michael Paquier questioned whether the module belongs in core.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Considering that this module could have a happier life if managed independently.

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_stat_statements: improve loading and saving routines for the dump file.
precedents_retrieved.summary: Change pg_stat_statements' dump-file save and load routines so that the trailing slock_t mutex field of pgssEntry is no longer written to or read from the file. The mutex would be required to stay the last field of the struct, with a comment saying so.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane found the gain negligible: it saves about 1.8% of the struct's on-disk size, and less once query texts are counted. He also said it adds no semantic correctness, because fread() reads into a transient local variable. He judged the savings not worth bumping the stats file magic number, which invalidates stored statistics. He also objected that requiring the mutex to be last removes the freedom to put it into padding later and makes the code more fragile.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
* The savings is not worth the costs of bumping the stats file format
magic number (and thereby invalidating everyone's stored statistics).

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Replace pg_restrict by standard restrict"
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Replace pg_restrict by standard restrict"
Reverted commit(s): Replace pg_restrict by standard restrict
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit f0f2c0c1aef95757c4e7f144d5577e2b0d814279.

The original problem that led to the use of pg_restrict was that MSVC
couldn't handle plain restrict, and defining it to something else
would conflict with its __declspec(restrict) that is used in system
header files.  In C11 mode, this is no longer a problem, as MSVC
handles plain restrict.  This led to the commit to replace pg_restrict
with restrict.  But this did not take C++ into account.  Standard C++
does not have restrict, so we defined it as something else (for
example, MSVC supports __restrict).  But this then again conflicts
with __declspec(restrict) in system header files.  So we have to
revert this attempt.  The comments are updated to clarify that the
reason for this is now C++ only.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert refactoring of restore command code to shell_restore.c
precedents_retrieved.summary: Revert refactoring of restore command code to shell_restore.c
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commits 24c35ec and 57169ad.  PreRestoreCommand() and
PostRestoreCommand() need to be put closer to the system() call calling
a restore_command, as they enable in_restore_command for the startup
process which would in turn trigger an immediate proc_exit() in the
SIGTERM handler.  Perhaps we could get rid of this behavior entirely,
but 24c35ec has made the window where the flag is enabled much larger
than it was, and any Postgres-like actions (palloc, etc.) taken by code
paths while the flag is enabled could lead to more severe issues in the
shutdown processing.

Note that curculio has showed that there are much more problems in this
area, unrelated to this change, actually, hence the issues related to
that had better be addressed first.  Keeping the code of HEAD in line
with the stable branches should make that a bit easier.

Per discussion with Andres Freund and Nathan Bossart.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found: the corpus search returned no earlier attempt at this idea. Message #4 points to the commit that introduced $libdir/plugins, but it does not say that a bare-name LOAD was proposed or rejected then. Without a recorded earlier rejection, this angle has no reason to apply. The role-dependent resolution concern in message #6 belongs to the design angle.
The error-message and SQLSTATE change was raised in message #6 and accepted with documentation in message #8, so it is not raised here. The proposal does not touch pg_dump, psql, GUCs or SQL syntax.

The proposal changes only how a non-superuser LOAD resolves a bare file name at run time. It adds no on-disk, WAL, catalog, wire protocol or replication state, and the material does not show a changed load_file() signature that would affect extensions. The role-dependent resolution and the changed error message belong to other angles.

The patch gives non-superusers no new privilege. A bare name expands to $libdir/plugins/name, which they could already LOAD with the explicit prefix, and message #5 reports that /tmp, $libdir and ../ paths are still rejected. The new "could not access file" error leaks nothing new, because the explicit-prefix form already gave the same answer. The role-dependent resolution in message #6 is a semantics issue, not an escalation: superusers can load either file anyway. Without the code, two points could not be checked: how a "bare" name is detected, including Windows separators, and whether dynamic_library_path is ever consulted.
No hot-path, ABI or external-dependency concern is visible from the prose. The change is small and touches only dfmgr.c and miscinit.c.
One objection from this angle: the explicit prefix already gives non-superusers the same result, and no extension or other mechanism is needed.
One demand objection. The rest of the thread concerns semantics and error codes, which other angles cover.
